items.reason: Artifacts assigns type "exploration" and orders it between spec and progress.
The dashboard consumes the same ordered artifact list.
The orphan check exempts exploration.md, with registration coverage.
Other validation rules and unlisted-markdown rejection remain intact.
Manifest.Explores reads the set-level explore boolean.
Exploration requires literal true; absent and false remain disabled.
ExplorerOverride reads agents and effort through the shared AgentDirective.
The guide documents both keys and explicitly distinguishes opt-in from opt-out.
The guide states the shared-seam and dependent-later-task rule.
Shared constants supply the names, with guide/accessor and filename assertions.
The command starts an Explorer with the task listing, task bodies, and available spec.
The prompt requests all five required aspects of the existing code.
The prompt requires checkable claims, approximately one page, and the observed tree.
The requested report structure contains no prior-art section or research requirement.
Successful passes atomically replace the flat exploration.md file.
Explore has its own captured-run phase, spend bucket, and retry-cap accounting.
Manual exploration bypasses manifest participation and the machine enable switch.
Failed, timed-out, and interrupted runs return before report replacement.
The command integration test checks the spawned agent, report replacement, and Explore stream row.
Both implementation paths conditionally add the report path and explanation.
Implementation prompts receive only the path, never report contents.
The prompt limits edits to correcting lines falsified by the current attempt.
The edit boundary explicitly permits the exploration report beside the task file.
The existing prior-art block is unchanged.
Assist receives the exploration pointer between refinement context and recent progress.
Golden tests cover implement and assist prompts with and without reports.
The drain invokes explorePhase before selecting its first task.
An existing report bypasses exploration and its agent spending.
Undeclared sets bypass the explore phase.
The separate work.explore group defaults enabled when its group or key is absent.
The machine switch disables automatic exploration without disabling the manual command.
Resolution follows CLI flags, manifest directive, then configured defaults.
explorePhase explicitly skips human-completed sets.
Report reuse depends on presence, with no recorded-tree comparison.
Whole-drain tests cover missing and existing reports and assert which phases ran.
The shared fallback walk retries using the standard cap and retry delays.
Failed captured exploration without a report derives EXPLORE-FAILED and stops draining.
Parking derives from captured-run metadata and report absence without schema changes.
EXPLORE-FAILED is distinct from BLOCKED, whose derivation remains unchanged.
READY-only daemon and automatic ready selection exclude parked rows.
attendableHITLTaskSets ignores row status and can select a parked set with an eligible HITL task.
A failed manual explore can park a set without a progress record; only the drain failure path records one.
--skip-explore bypasses exploration and permits an explicitly targeted parked set to drain.
Report creation or removal of the declaration clears the derived park.
CONTEXT.md lists EXPLORE-FAILED among drain stops and automatic-selection exclusions.
Unexplored sets carry a separate mark and explanatory reason.
ResolveExploreMark returns no mark for undeclared sets.
Refresh resolves the mark centrally and propagates it to all four surfaces.
Parked rows retain their exploration mark in dashboard and Work status cells.
explorationParts suppresses the path-and-tree pointer for manually explored sets without an explore declaration.
The sign-off gate places the exploration pointer and reading action beside refinement.
ResolveExploreMark treats any non-interrupted captured run, including success, as failure when the report disappears.

scores.rationale: Clear shared mechanisms and substantial tests, but parking recovery, HITL selection, progress recording, and undeclared-report display have gaps.
